q: In what year was Volusia County created?
f: The Florida Legislature carved Volusia out of Orange County on December 29, 1854.

q: Which city has been the Volusia County seat since 1887?
f: Enterprise was the first county seat. DeLand took over in 1887 and still holds it.

q: Who founded the 1768 colony of New Smyrna?
f: Dr. Andrew Turnbull named it for Smyrna, the Aegean city where his wife was born.

q: Most of the 1,400+ New Smyrna colonists came from which island?
f: Survivors marched to St. Augustine in 1777 and became Florida's Minorcan community.

q: How tall is the Ponce de Leon Inlet Lighthouse, Florida's tallest?
f: First lit in 1887, it stands 175 feet tall at the south end of Ponce Inlet.

q: In 1904 Mary McLeod Bethune opened her Daytona school with how much money?
f: She started with $1.50 and five girls. The school grew into Bethune-Cookman University.

q: NASCAR was organized in 1947 at which Daytona Beach hotel?
f: Bill France Sr. hosted the meetings in the rooftop Ebony Club starting December 14, 1947.

q: How fast did Sir Malcolm Campbell drive Blue Bird on Daytona sand in 1935?
f: He hit 276.82 mph on March 7, 1935. Record runs soon moved to the Bonneville Salt Flats.

q: Bike Week began in 1937 with which race?
f: Ed Kretz won the first Daytona 200 on a beach-and-road course riding an Indian.
The Daytona Beach visitors bureau created the October rally in 1991.

q: Where did Jackie Robinson play his first integrated spring game in 1946?
f: The City Island ballpark welcomed him on March 17, 1946. It is now Jackie Robinson Ballpark.

q: Daytona Beach is named after which founder?
f: Mathias Day of Ohio bought the land in 1870, and the town took his name.

q: Which nearby city calls itself the Birthplace of Speed?
f: Early automobile speed trials ran on the hard-packed Ormond-Daytona beach from 1903.

q: In what year was the first Daytona 500 held?
f: Lee Petty won the first Daytona 500 in 1959, the year the Speedway opened.

q: Stetson University in DeLand is named for a maker of what?
f: Hat maker John B. Stetson backed the school, founded as DeLand Academy in 1883.
